subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the nth term of an arithmetic sequence with first term a and common difference d?
questions.explain: Each term adds one further common difference, so the nth term is a + (n - 1)d.

questions.q: In an arithmetic sequence, the constant amount added to get from one term to the next is called the:
questions.explain: Arithmetic sequences increase or decrease by a fixed common difference each term.

questions.q: Find the nth term rule for the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, ...
questions.explain: The common difference is 4 and 4(1) - 1 = 3, matching the first term.

questions.q: A sequence has nth term 4n - 1. What is the 20th term?
questions.explain: Substituting n = 20 gives 4(20) - 1 = 79.

questions.q: What is the nth term of a geometric sequence with first term a and common ratio r?
questions.explain: Each term multiplies by r, so the nth term is the first term times r^(n-1).

questions.q: For two functions f and g, what does the composite function fg(x) mean?
questions.explain: In fg(x) the function g is applied first, then f is applied to the result.

questions.q: What does the notation f⁻¹(x) represent?
questions.explain: f⁻¹ is the inverse function, which reverses the effect of f.

questions.q: If f(x) = 2x + 1, what is f(3)?
questions.explain: Substituting x = 3 gives 2(3) + 1 = 7.

questions.q: If f(x) = x² and g(x) = x + 3, what is fg(x)?
If f(x) = 3x - 2 and g(x) = x + 4, what is fg(1)?
Find the inverse function f⁻¹(x) of f(x) = 2x - 6.
questions.explain: Setting y = 2x - 6 and rearranging for x gives f⁻¹(x) = (x + 6)/2.

questions.q: In the straight-line equation y = mx + c, what does m represent?
questions.explain: In y = mx + c, m is the gradient (steepness) of the line.

questions.q: In the straight-line equation y = mx + c, what does c represent?
questions.explain: c is the value of y where the line crosses the y-axis.

questions.q: What is the gradient of the line passing through (1, 2) and (3, 8)?
What is the shape of the graph of y = x²?
questions.explain: A quadratic function such as y = x² produces a U-shaped parabola.

questions.q: The graph of y = 1/x is an example of which type of graph?
questions.explain: y = 1/x is a reciprocal function, giving a two-branch reciprocal curve.

questions.q: A straight line passes through (0, 4) and (2, 10). What is its equation?
questions.explain: The gradient is (10 - 4)/(2 - 0) = 3 and the y-intercept is 4.

questions.q: If y = xⁿ, what is dy/dx?
questions.explain: Differentiating a power multiplies by the index and reduces the power by one.

questions.q: Differentiate y = x³ with respect to x.
questions.explain: Multiply by the power 3 and reduce the index by one to get 3x².

questions.q: For the curve y = x² - 4x + 1, what is the gradient when x = 3?
questions.explain: dy/dx = 2x - 4, so at x = 3 the gradient is 2(3) - 4 = 2.
